name: Speech pacing apps
lead: Speech pacing apps are software tools that people use to practice the speed and pauses of their speaking. Pace is of interest in appearance and presence culture because listeners form impressions from it. Researchers distinguish speaking rate, which includes pauses, from articulation rate, which excludes them, and typical English speech runs at about four syllables per second, with a range of roughly 3.3 to 5.9 depending on context.[1]

Linguist Howard Giles found that faster speakers of several English accents were rated as more competent, though judging tempo is described as open to subjective bias.[1] No published trial has tested whether pacing apps change such impressions.

card.summary: Apps for practicing speaking speed; pace affects impressions, but the apps themselves are untested.
card.note: No trials of pacing apps found.

quick.overview:
Pacing apps help people monitor and practice how fast and evenly they speak.

Speech-tempo research links perceived speed with perceived competence, but no studies test the apps.
quick.mechanism: Users record or speak while the app tracks pace, then adjust speed and pauses.
